findings.title: Double- or triple-click to select a name still toggles the row once
findings.body:
The guard works for drag-select, because the text is already selected when the click fires. A double-click (select a word) or triple-click (select the whole name) sends a separate `click` for each press. The first click comes before anything is selected, so `getSelection()` is empty and the row toggles. Only the later clicks are skipped. Before this change a double-click toggled twice and the row ended where it started. Now it ends flipped, so copying a name by double- or triple-click still unticks the row as a side effect.

One option: ignore a click when `event.detail > 1`. That doesn't undo the first toggle, though. If you want to cover these cases, you could toggle on `mouseup` only when nothing is selected, or delay the toggle until the double-click window has passed. You may decide this is fine, since the row's dimmed state does show the change.

contracts.action: Row click is skipped while the document has a non-empty text selection
contracts.equivalent_path: Checkbox onChange (setFixing with the box's checked value) and the existing input-target early return
contracts.before_after: Before: any click on the row that wasn't on the input called setFixing([path], !fixing). After: the same, except when window.getSelection() has text at click time. In that case nothing changes.
contracts.visible_effect: The row keeps its checked or dimmed state after a drag-select. For a double- or triple-click, the first click still toggles (before anything is selected) and the later ones are skipped, so the row ends flipped.
contracts.failure_mode: Synchronous DOM read with no async work. getSelection() returning null is handled by `?.`, so the toggle proceeds.

thread_replies.reply: Confirmed: line 216 now skips the toggle when there's selected text, and the test at lines 368-374 checks it. That covers drag-select. One smaller gap is left: with a double- or triple-click, the first click toggles before anything is selected. I've noted that separately as a consider.
